question.text: A PM holds a Rs. 50 cr portfolio with 20 well-diversified stocks. Adding the 21st uncorrelated stock will:

answer.text: Reduce unsystematic risk significantly — largest marginal benefit
Reduce risk marginally (law of diminishing returns)

explanation.text: The Logic: Diversification benefit follows diminishing returns. Past 30-35 stocks, additions have minimal effect. At 20 stocks, meaningful but much smaller than the first 10. The Trap: Systematic risk can't be diversified away; 'eliminate all risk' is wrong. Cross-Exam Context: Core MPT; XXI-B Topic 15 treats this formally with efficient frontier. Manager's Pro-Tip: Most PMS portfolios run 25-40 stocks — balancing diversification with conviction-sizing.
